question: The value of cosec 30° − cos 60° is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute standard trigonometric values from the table.

cosec 30° = 2

cos 60° = 1/2

Calculation: 2 − 1/2 = 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: cosec 30° − cos 60°

Formula used: Standard values of trigonometric ratios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/735b3eb7bba87cd80fd8ff5b96896d5dd2561ec0619a57d19d1bc545fc9a2032.png] 

⇒ cosec 30° = 1 ÷ sin 30°

⇒ Since sin 30° = 1/2, then cosec 30° = 1 ÷ (1/2) = 2

⇒ From the standard table, cos 60° = 1/2

⇒ Substitute these values into the expression:

⇒ 2 − 1/2

⇒ (4 − 1) ÷ 2

⇒ 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric functions have reciprocal pairs: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Complementary Angles

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ). Thus, sin 30° = cos(90° − 30°) = cos 60° = 1/2.

Standard Trigonometric Values

Important values to remember: sin 0°=0, sin 30°=1/2, sin 45°=1/√2, sin 60°=√3/2, sin 90°=1.</p
